newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Renault reports big loss.
newsitem.headline: France's Renault reports big loss.

text.p: French carmaker Renault on Thursday said it made a net attributable loss of 5.25 billion francs ($923.3 million) in 1996, its first loss in a decade, after taking hefty charges for the planned closure of its Belgian Vilvoorde plant and job cuts in France.
Renault, which made a profit the previous year of 2.14 billion francs, said it took charges in 1996 of 3.91 billion francs. ($ = 5.686 French Francs)
Chairman Louis Schweitzer told reporters he expected Renault to show an operating profit in 1997, but said the net result would depend on exceptional items.
Earlier, striking Belgian Renault workers clashed with French police outside a compound in northern France where thousands of cars are stored, witnesses said.

Paramilitary gendarmes protecting the site at Wavrin, south of the city of Lille, fired tear gas after being stoned by some 400 workers from Vilvoorde in the Brussels suburbs. Renault has said it will close the Vilvoorde plant in July with the loss of 3,100 jobs.
Schweitzer, who met Belgian unions on Wednesday, has said Renault's decision to close the plant is irrevocable.
